html:
SMTO-CTX-0036 — A task note changed before it could be updated

GUID: d7073799-5e65-5d3c-83ef-b713f7662e52
Slug: task-context-revision-conflict
Domain: CTX · Subsystem: task-context

What happened

  • Something changed a task note or saved message after it was last read, so SMTO refused to save over it. This keeps the newer version from being lost. The change you or the task tried to make was not saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were using Save to task context on a message, refresh the page so you see the message's latest text. The message changed after the page showed it, so SMTO needs you to save the current version.
  2. Look at the button on that message. If it already shows Saved · Remove, your save is there. If it shows Save to task context, select it again. The earlier save was refused, but checking first avoids saving the same thing twice.
  3. If the task itself hit this while updating its notes, let it continue; it is told to read the latest note and update that. The task can merge its change into the newer note without losing either version.

What success looks like

  • The message shows Saved · Remove, or the task's notes update and the task carries on.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't try to force an older version over the newer one; that would throw away the newer changes.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Task Context write was rejected because the notebook entry, note, book, source or saved message selection no longer matches the revision the caller read (for example book_revision_conflict, note_revision_conflict, source_changed or saved_message_source_changed).

What this means

  • The notebook entry or saved selection changed since it was read. The recorded reason and operation message identify the specific condition.

Why this can happen

  • A notebook note, book, source or selection changed relative to the observed version.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the operation, reason, revision and source reference recorded by the producer.

How to fix it

  • Read the current entry or selection, compare it with the expected_revision and current_revision recorded in the error, merge the intended change, and write again with the current revision. Do not bypass the revision check or overwrite the newer content.
  • Read the current entry or selection, reconcile the changes, and use its current revision.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the indicated argument or refresh the source first; retain existing access checks and revision checks.

How to verify the fix

  • The corrected notebook operation succeeds.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass source access checks or overwrite a revision conflict.

Technical notes

  • An unavailable source does not prove that no relevant information exists.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors
